own.bio: Strange but true stories, told quietly. New odd hour, every week.

posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

recentPosts.caption: What if continents and oceans switched places? The Pacific becomes a supercontinent. Earth's deepest point is Everest Deep, and is almost nine kilometers below sea-level. And the Mid-Atlantic Canyon divides the world from pole to pole. Life finds a way but struggles in this new, upside-down world. This all sounds cool, until the oxygen runs out.

Pigeons are basically GPS Drones with superpowers. They can pinpoint their own location hundreds of kilometers from their roosts and navigate home autonomously, only using smell, the Sun, and even Earth’s magnetic field.

No one works harder than our rover driver Yolk, who is tirelessly collecting nuggets every day so that the space station can function smoothly.

Have you already started your space adventure? Star Birds, which we developed together with our friends at @toukana_interactive, is available on Steam!
Two billion years ago, the world’s first nuclear reactors appeared in Oklo, Gabon. They were NOT made by humans and were self-regulating and accident-free.

In the late 9th century, Vikings have raided kingdom after kingdom and nearly conquered all of England. Wealthy monasteries and defenseless nuns were especially tempting targets and often suffered great losses. However, all of that stopped when Vikings were confronted by princess Aethelflaed, daughter of Alfred the Great.

Who was Lady of Mercia, and how did she shape the history of England by becoming Vikings' greatest nightmare? Watch our latest Nightshift video to find out! 🌚
Laughing gas can make you feel relaxed and euphoric in seconds. But it comes with serious risks as well. So, what exactly is laughing gas and why does it feel so good?

In the 17th century in Germany, one of Europe’s most terrifying witch hunts turned the town of Bamberg against itself. Tortures that occurred in the "Witch Factory" forced innocent people to name friends, neighbors and family members, creating a deadly chain reaction that eventually reached even the richest and most powerful, while those running the trials profited from the people they condemned.

How did a witch hunt grow so powerful that almost nobody was safe? And what finally brought one of
What if you could skip the boring and painful parts of life? It sounds tempting until you realize what you’d lose along the way. Time doesn’t really stop, and neither does the world.
Brace yourself... 😔

We’re not looking for the usual suspects like Capricorn, Gemini or Scorpio. We want weird, creative, charming, ridiculous or completely made-up constellations instead.

Got an idea? Drop your constellation names in the comments! Our favorite suggestions might actually make it into the game.

competitors.bio: Discover the most incredible experiences from around the world 🌎✈️ Business: info@damiermedia.com

recentPosts.caption:
@memory_chasers takes us around the world to 8 unforgettable stays, from sleeping inside an ice room in Sweden and an igloo beneath the Matterhorn to watching the Northern Lights from bed in Iceland and sharing a private desert pool with wandering gazelles in Dubai. 🧊🏔️🦌⁠
⁠
Other highlights include a jungle-inspired hotel in Greece, a luxury camp beneath the stars in Wadi Rum, architect-designed treehouses in Sweden, and a volcanic retreat at Iceland’s Blue Lagoon.⁠
Which one would you choose

This beach in Iceland looks like it’s covered in diamonds. ❄️⁠
⁠
Huge pieces of glacier ice wash up along the black volcanic sand, with some so clear they almost look like glass. The waves move them along the shore, so the beach can look completely different from one visit to the next.⁠
⁠
It’s one of those places that looks almost unreal in person.⁠
⁠
Would you visit it?

Homemade buns coming straight out of a balcony in Oslo? Now that’s a pop-up worth waiting for. 🥐🏠✨⁠
This delicious little experience, where freshly baked cinnamon and cardamom buns are handed out directly from the balcony, turning a simple bakery stop into a fun interaction with the people behind it.⁠
⁠
Would you line up for one? 👀⁠
🎥: @sourdough.etc

Guccio Gucci worked at The Savoy in the late 1800s, long before his name became synonymous with luxury fashion. ⁠
⁠
The hotel later became part of that story in another way with its Gucci Royal Suite, where the brand’s style meets The Savoy’s classic London elegance. ⁠
⁠
Today, that connection lives on in the Gucci Royal Suite, one of the hotel’s most distinctive spaces, while The Savoy itself remains one of London’s most famous hotels. ⁠
⁠
From its elegant interiors and Thames views to its icon

This Airbnb looks like a dream in the middle of the jungle. 🌴✨⁠
A dreamy jungle escape where incredible architecture meets nature, complete with two private jungle cenotes, a padel court, and stunning design.⁠
⁠
The kind of stay where the accommodation itself becomes the destination. 🏡💦🌿⁠
🎥: @artexperiences_re @rocioyacobane

Tivoli Gardens just created a little Japanese neighborhood in the heart of Copenhagen. ⁠
⁠
The new area takes inspiration from the streets of Japan, with neon signs, lanterns, architecture, food spots, and shops.⁠
⁠
Materials are brought from Japan, including more than 60 tonnes of bricks, along with doors, windows, and plants.⁠
⁠
For anyone who loves Japanese culture, this is a great way to experience its traditions, design, and everyday details. ⁠
⁠
Would you visit Hikari? 👀 ⁠
⁠
By: @tivolicp

This tiny frog in Costa Rica looks like it walked straight out of a Spider-Man movie. 🕷️🐸⁠
⁠
Photographer @jwinden_macro captured this strawberry poison dart frog (Oophaga pumilio) at Centro Manu in Costa Rica. The species is known for its bright color combinations, including the red body and blue legs seen here.⁠

One of the most scenic ways to experience Kyoto from the water. 🚣‍♀️🌿🇯🇵⁠
The Arashiyama river boat ride takes you through the beautiful landscapes around Kyoto, offering a peaceful view of the surrounding mountains and forest.⁠
⁠
And the best part? Local vendors on the boats sell traditional Japanese snacks along the way, making the journey even more fun. 🍡✨⁠
🎥: @aannie.pham

Botín has been serving traditional Spanish food in the heart of Madrid since 1725, making it the world’s oldest continuously operating restaurant according to Guinness World Records.⁠
⁠
The restaurant is known for its roast suckling pig and lamb, still prepared in its wood-fired oven, which dates back to its beginnings. Its four floors also preserve much of the old inn-like atmosphere that has been part of Botín for centuries.⁠
⁠
Even Ernest Hemingway was a fan; he mentioned Botín in The Sun Als

Carved straight into the rose-colored cliffs, Petra is one of the world’s most extraordinary ancient cities. 🤩⁠
⁠
Known as the “Rose City,” this UNESCO World Heritage Site was once a major trading hub of the Nabataean Kingdom. Its most famous landmark, the Treasury, was carved directly into the sandstone more than 2,000 years ago.⁠
🎥: @ekaterina_argunova

Kisshoin Tenmangu has stood in Kyoto since 934 and is dedicated to Sugawara no Michizane, a Shinto deity associated with learning and wisdom. Today, the shrine also has a Sanrio collaboration, with special Hello Kitty omamori, fortune slips, and goshuin.⁠
⁠
The character details are subtle enough to spot as you explore the shrine, which makes the visit even more fun. ⁠
⁠
Just keep in mind that some of the Hello Kitty items are seasonal or limited and may not always be available.⁠
⁠
By: @mar1kuma

Imagine heading to lunch in Stockholm and accidentally walking into a full-on street parade. 😂⁠
While exploring Gamla Stan, these travelers came across a lively Catalan cultural parade filled with colorful costumes, music, and plenty of energy.⁠
⁠
A completely unexpected encounter, and definitely one way to make a simple lunch break memorable. 🎭✨⁠
🎥: @carolinestromstedts @fab.lefou

On safari in the Pantanal, photographer @sandesh_kadur noticed a black vulture in the middle of the water. "I wasn't sure what was going on, so our amazing Boat Guide, Branco, veered towards the vulture. That’s when I saw a dead caiman floating on the water's surface. The single vulture that had landed on it was trying in desperation to feed on the carcass, but the log-rolling caiman proved to be quite the challenge—like trying to eat while on a treadmill."

New cat alert! A call from a wildlife sanctuary about a "weird cat" has led to the first new cat species discovered in over 100 years. Smaller than an average housecat and covered in leopard-like spots, the cat species—proposed name Leopardus tilcayo—lives in Bolivia’s Yungas forest ecoregion, and very little is known about its day-to-day life in the wild. This photo was featured in our @natgeoyourshot #NatGeoYourShotDiscoveries challenge.

One in seven adults says they've lost money to a romance scam. @marianavz is using her investigative skills to explore these devastating scams from the inside out, unraveling the tricks scammers use to draw in their victims and make them fall so deeply in love they'll give away their hearts—and their money.

#SuperScamMe premieres Saturday, October 17 at 9/8c on National Geographic. Streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Think you need to hit 10,000 steps every day to make your walk count? New research suggests there’s another way to get more from your daily stroll: pick up the pace. Find out what scientists discovered about the relationship between step count, walking intensity, and health at the link in bio. 

Photograph by Tatiana Maksimova, Getty

Summer school looks a little different for loon chicks. During their first 12 weeks, they learn essential survival skills from their parents, including how to swim, dive, and forage.

#InsideTheEnchantedWaterways is now streaming on @DisneyPlus

Fishing guide Justin Dymond spends his nights taking bowfishers out on Florida's Crystal River. But he's not the only one hunting. Bottlenose dolphins gather around his boat, using its lights to find and flush prey from hiding places—the first documented partnership of this kind in the United States. The relationship has changed how Dymond sees the cetaceans he once considered competition, and after years of watching it develop, he turned to National Geographic Explorer Stefanie Gazda to better

Photo by @jake_brass | I captured this image, “Three Beaks,” while visiting the Saltee Islands in Ireland. When these puffins began to line up, I saw the potential for a quirky image of a puffin tower and positioned myself accordingly. I was fortunate that they all posed differently, creating this unique puffin stack.

This photo was featured in our @natgeoyourshot #NatGeoYourShotOurHOME challenge.
